name: codebase-tour
description: Get a newcomer (a new engineer, or the agent itself) oriented in an unfamiliar repository before they make one specific change, with a short tour scoped to that change. It gives the install, run and test commands taken from CI, package scripts and the Makefile; the path the change touches, traced through the code with file:line citations; where the change goes; the conventions the code actually follows; the traps (generated files, a second copy of the logic, untested code, env vars, flags); and a first step that can be checked. Use when someone says "I'm new to this repo", "get me oriented", "where would I make this change", "walk me through the code for X", "onboard me before I start this ticket", or "how do I run and test this".

handoff.when: the tour names where the change goes and a first step
handoff.purpose: Implement the change against acceptance criteria, starting from the tour's first step and running the area's test command it found.
handoff.fallback: If feature-implement-loop is absent, take the tour's first step: write the failing test it names, run the area's test command before and after the change, and update every place listed under 'Must change with it'.

permissions.notes: scripts/repo_facts.py reads files under the repository root it is given and prints to stdout. It writes nothing and runs no commands.

model.rationale: Reading a repo and citing what it finds is generation over evidence; every claim is checked against a file, so a mid tier is enough.
